{{short description|Russian basketball player (born 2006)}} {{Infobox basketball biography | name = Egor Dëmin
Егор Дёмин | image = Egor Demin - BYU Blue vs. White 2024 (cropped).jpg | alt = | caption = Dëmin with [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] in 2024 | position = [[Point guard]]/[[Shooting guard]] | height_ft = 6 | height_in = 9 | weight_lb = 200 | league = [[National Basketball Association|NBA]] | team = Brooklyn Nets | number = 8 | birth_date = {{birth date and age|2006|3|3|df=y}} | birth_place = [[Moscow]], Russia | high_school = | college = [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]] (2024–2025) | draft_year = 2025 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 8 | draft_team = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = 2023 | team1 = [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] | years2 = {{nbay|2025|start}}–present | team2 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | highlights = * [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team (2025) }} '''Egor Vladimirovich Dëmin''' ({{IPAc-en|j|ɪ|ˈ|g|ɔːr|_|ˈ|d|j|oʊ|m|ɪ|n}} {{respell|yih|GOR|_|DYOH|min}}; Russian: Егор Владимирович Дёмин, {{IPA|ru|jɪˈgor ˈdʲɵmʲɪn}}; born 3 March 2006) is a Russian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Brooklyn Nets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU Cougars]]. He previously played for [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]]. He also represents the [[Russia men's national basketball team|Russian national team]]. ==Early life== Dëmin was born on 3 March 2006.{{Cite web|url=https://basketball.eurobasket.com/player/Egor-Demin/617738|website=[[Eurobasket.com]]|title=Egor Demin}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.heraldextra.com/sports/byu/2024/jun/17/on-his-way-russian-star-egor-demin-officially-signs-with-byu-mens-basketball/|newspaper=[[Daily Herald (Utah)|Daily Herald]]|title=On his way: Russian star Egor Demin officially signs with BYU men's basketball|date=17 June 2024|author=Dickson, Darnell}} His father, Vladimir, was also a basketball player.{{Cite web|url=https://30-under-30.forbes.ru/2024/510307-egor-demin|website=[[Forbes|Forbes Russia]]|title=Егор Демин, 18 {{!}} Номинация «Спорт и киберспорт|language=Russian|trans-title=Egor Demin, 18 {{!}} Nomination “Sports and eSports”|date=2024}} He grew up in [[Moscow]] and attended the Moscow Basketball Academy (also known as the Trinta School) where he trained until 2021.{{Cite web|url=https://mba.mossport.ru/news/egor-demin-chempion-yunosheskoy-evroligi/|website=MosSport.ru|title=Егор Демин - чемпион юношеской Евролиги!|date=22 May 2023|trans-title=Egor Demin is the champion of the Junior Euroleague!|language=Russian}} He received offers to play with other teams, including [[BC Khimki]], but opted to stay at the academy until age 15 to be with his coach, Evgeny Gorbunov. Dëmin sent highlight footage to European teams and received six offers by 2021. He was considered a top Russian prospect and signed a six-year contract with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] in Spain in September 2021, at age 15.{{Cite web|url=https://www.defensacentral.com/baloncesto/1630589830-oficial-el-real-madrid-ha-fichado-al-mayor-talento-de-rusia-el-joven-egor-demin|website=DefensaCentral.com|title=Oficial: el Real Madrid ha fichado al mayor talento de Rusia, el joven Egor Demin|date=2 September 2021|author=Casado, Ramón|language=Spanish|trans-title=Official: Real Madrid has signed the greatest talent in Russia, the young Egor Demin}} Playing for the cadet "A" team in the Real Madrid academy, he helped them win the Spanish Cadet Championship in 2022 while averaging 17.3 points and 4.3 rebounds in the tournament.{{Cite news|url=https://www.sport-express.ru/basketball/euroleague/reviews/basketbol-kto-takoy-egor-demin-luchshiy-rossiyskiy-igrok-posle-kirilenko-skolko-emu-let-1931313/|newspaper=[[Sport Express]]|title="Его лично курирует агент Дончича". Российский разыгрывающий зажигает в "Реале"|date=26 May 2022|author=Ganeev, Timur|language=Russian|trans-title=“He is personally supervised by Doncic’s agent.” Russian point guard lights up Real Madrid}} For the following two seasons, he was a member of the junior "A" team and the [[Real Madrid Baloncesto B|Real Madrid B]] team in the [[Tercera FEB|Liga EBA]].{{Cite news|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/06/11/byu-recruit-egor-demin-byu-star-traveled-similar-paths/|newspaper=[[Deseret News]]|title=BYU's former Russian basketball star sees big things ahead for Cougars' top prospect|date=11 June 2024|author=McCann, Dave}} Dëmin helped Real Madrid B to the [[Euroleague Basketball Next Generation Tournament]] championship in 2023 and scored 10 points in the final, while finishing with averages of 8.5 points and 6.8 rebounds per game. In May 2023, he received a promotion to the main Real Madrid squad and made his debut at the age of 17, playing in just one game there.{{Cite web|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/242530/egor-demin|website=Proballers.com|title=Egor Demin}} With Real Madrid B in the 2023–24 season, he played 21 games and averaged 13 points and 5.1 rebounds per game. He also helped Real Madrid B return to the Next Generation Tournament and scored double figures in all four games, including 26 points and 11 rebounds in the final, an 85–84 overtime win over the French academy [[INSEP]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.sports.ru/basketball/1116097542-egor-demin-stal-dvukratnym-chempionom-yuniorskoj-evroligi.html|website=Sports.ru|title=Егор Демин стал двукратным чемпионом юниорской Евролиги|language=Russian|trans-title=Egor Demin became a two-time champion of the Junior Euroleague|date=26 May 2024|author=Ilyin, Gennady}} In 2024, Dëmin was one of the nominees for the Russian [[Forbes 30 Under 30|''Forbes'' 30 Under 30]] list. ===Recruiting=== Following the 2023–24 season, Dëmin opted to move to the U.S. to play [[college basketball]].{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/college/byu/basketball/international-nba-prospect-egor-demin-commits-to-byu-basketball|magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]|title=International NBA Prospect Egor Demin Commits to BYU Basketball|date=28 May 2024|author=Lundquist, Casey}} He committed to playing college basketball for [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|BYU]], where he was the program’s first five-star recruit;{{cite web | title=Egor Demin is now officially the highest-rated recruit in BYU history | date=2 August 2024 | url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/08/02/byu-egor-demin-five-star/ }} he was described in the ''[[Deseret News]]'' as "arguably the most notable prospect ever to commit to the BYU basketball program."{{Cite news|url=https://www.deseret.com/sports/2024/06/02/egor-demin-announces-commitment-to-byu-basketball/|access-date=October 22, 2025|newspaper=[[Deseret News]]|title='Let's rock BYU': Russian star Egor | On3 overall = 34 | espn overall = N/A | accessdate = 20 July 2024 | bball = yes }} ==College career== As a freshman, Dëmin averaged 10.6 points, 5.5 assists, 3.9 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game. He was selected to the [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] All-Freshman Team. Following the season, Dëmin declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{cite news |title=BYU freshman Egor Demin to announce draft decision |url=https://kwsn.com/2025/04/08/byu-freshman-egor-demin-to-announce-draft-decision/ |access-date=December 17, 2025 |work=KWSN |date=April 8, 2025}} ==Professional career== Dëmin was selected with the 8th overall pick by the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in the [[2025 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |title=2025 NBA Draft Results: Picks 1-59 {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2025-nba-draft-order |access-date=11 July 2025 |website=NBA |language=en}} He was signed on 3 July 2025.{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Egor Dëmin, Ben Saraf and Danny Wolf {{!}} Brooklyn Nets |url=https://brooklynnets.com/news/brooklyn-nets-sign-egor-demin-ben-saraf-and-danny-wolf |access-date=11 July 2025 |website=brooklynnets.com |language=en}} During a loss to the [[2025–26 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] on 29 December, Dëmin broke the Nets franchise record for most three pointers in a single game by a rookie, shooting 7-for-14 on the night.{{Cite web |date=2025-12-30 |title=Nets' Egor Demin Catches Fire From Three-Point Range in Loss to Warriors |url=https://www.si.com/nba/nets/onsi/news/nets-egor-demin-catches-fire-from-three-point-range-in-loss-to-warriors |access-date=2025-12-31 |website=Brooklyn Nets On SI |language=en-US}} On January 30, 2026, Dëmin made a three-pointer in his 34th straight game, breaking the NBA record for most consecutive games with a made three-pointer by a rookie. That night, he led the Nets with 25 points, 10 rebounds and 5 three-point field goals during a 106-99 win over the [[2025–26 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].{{Cite web|title=Nets guard Egor Demin sets NBA rookie record with 3-pointer|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/47783563/nets-guard-egor-demin-sets-nba-rookie-record-3-pointer|website=ESPN.com|date=January 31, 2026|access-date=January 31, 2026|language=en|first=|last=}} Dëmin made 52 appearances (including 45 starts) for Brooklyn during his rookie campaign, recording averages of 10.3 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 3.3 assists. On 9 March, Dëmin was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to increased [[plantar fasciitis]] in his left foot.{{Cite web|title=Nets' Egor Demin out for rest of season with injury in tough end to promising rookie campaign|url=https://nypost.com/2026/03/09/sports/nets-egor-demin-out-for-rest-of-season-with-plantar-fasciitis/|access-date=March 13, 2026|website=nypost.com|language=en}} Dëmin returned to the court during the [[2026 NBA Summer League]]. In Las Vegas, despite playing in only 3 of the Nets 5 games, Dëmin averaged 21 ppg and 4.3 apg en route to being named a second team All-Summer league performer.{{Cite web |last=Bergstrom |first=Bjorn |date=July 21, 2026 |title=Former BYU star Egor Demin leveled up at 2026 NBA Summer League |url=https://byucougarswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/college/cougars/mens-basketball/2026/07/21/byu-mens-basketball-egor-demin-nba-summer-league-superlative/90990582007/ |access-date=July 27, 2026 |website=BYU Cougars Wire |language=en-US}} ESPN also named Dëmin the "Best Sophomore" during Summer League.{{Cite web |last=Golliver |first=Ben |date=July 20, 2026 |title=NBA summer league superlatives: Which players impressed? |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/49391646/2026-2027-nba-summer-league-superlatives-mvp-aj-dybantsa-cameron-boozer-vegas |access-date=July 27, 2026 |website=www.espn.com}} ==National team career== Dëmin represented Russia at the [[2021 FIBA U16 European Challengers]] tournament where he had per-40-minute averages of 21.1 points and 6.9 rebounds.{{Cite news|url=https://en.as.com/en/2021/09/17/nba/1631870761_527152.html|newspaper=[[Diario AS]]|title=Real Madrid's Demin, Duru among youngsters tipped for NBA|date=17 September 2021|author=Faucha, Fernando}} His performance at the tournament received comparisons to [[Luka Dončić]] by [[ESPN]] journalist Mike Schmitz. ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== Source{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/d/demineg01.html|title=Egor Dёmin NBA stats|website=[[Basketball Reference]]|publisher=Sports Reference LLC|date=27 February 2026|accessdate=10 March 2026}} {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2025}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2025–26 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn]] | 52 || 45 || 25.2 || .399 || .385 || .831 || 3.2 || 3.3 || .8 || .3 || 10.3 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 52 || 45 || 25.2 || .399 || .385 || .831 || 3.2 || 3.3 || .8 || .3 || 10.3 {{S-end}} ===College=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[2024–25 BYU Cougars men's basketball team|BYU]] | 33 || 33 || 27.5 || .412 || .273 || .695 || 3.9 || 5.5 || 1.2 || .4 || 10.6 {{S-end}} ===Domestic leagues=== {| class="wikitable sortable" style="font-size:100%; text-align:right;" !
